catalyst_text: Announced positive topline Phase 3 results meeting endpoints
detailed_catalyst_text: Topline data from the pivotal Phase 3 APOLLO study in erythropoietic protoporphyria and X-linked protoporphyria met both co-primary endpoints and all secondary endpoints. Significant reductions in PPIX and meaningful increases in light tolerance were observed, alongside quality-of-life improvements. The therapy was generally well tolerated with no new safety signals reported.
catalyst_text_evidence: Disc Medicine, Inc. today announced topline results from the APOLLO Phase 3 trial of bitopertin in erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP), including X-linked protoporphyria (XLP). The trial met all its primary and secondary endpoints. All secondary endpoint results were also positive and statistically significant, including reductions in phototoxic reactions and improvements on multiple measures of light tolerance. Bitopertin achieved statistical significance on both co-primary endpoints vs. placebo: Reduction in whole-blood metal-free PPIX from baseline (-41.4% vs. placebo, p<0.0001) Increase in average monthly total time in light without pain during month 6 (+12.2 hours vs. placebo, p=0.0010). Bitopertin was generally well-tolerated with no new safety signals observed in APOLLO.

catalyst_text: Presented positive initial Phase 2 results at conference
detailed_catalyst_text: Initial positive results from the Phase 2 RESTORE-PV trial of DISC-3405 in polycythemia vera were presented at a scientific meeting, showing increased hepcidin, lowered serum iron, reduced phlebotomy, controlled hematocrit, and improved symptom burden. These findings indicate meaningful clinical activity in PV and support continued development of the program.
catalyst_text_evidence: Disc Medicine, Inc. (NASDAQ:IRON), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of novel treatments for patients suffering from serious hematologic diseases, today presented positive initial results from the RESTORE-PV Phase 2 trial of DISC-3405 in patients with polycythemia vera (PV). The data, presented in a poster session at the 2026 Society of Hematologic Oncology (SOHO) annual meeting in Houston, TX, demonstrated that treatment with DISC-3405 increased hepcidin and lowered serum iron, translating to reduction in phlebotomy, controlled hematocrit, and improved symptom burden in patients with PV.

catalyst_text: Reported favorable Phase 2 long term EPP data
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated Phase 2 HELIOS open-label extension data in erythropoietic protoporphyria showed sustained reductions in protoporphyrin IX and significant improvements in light tolerance on continued dosing. Favorable longer-term safety with up to 2.5+ years of exposure supports durability of effect and continued development.
catalyst_text_evidence: Updated data from the HELIOS open-label extension trial of bitopertin in EPP, to be presented in a poster session tomorrow, 2026-06-13, show sustained reductions in PPIX, significant improvement in light tolerance measures, and favorable longer-term safety in patients treated with bitopertin. HELIOS is an ongoing Phase 2, open-label, long-term extension trial that enrolled 86 adult and adolescent patients with EPP from the BEACON and AURORA trials. Longer term treatment with bitopertin was associated with sustained reductions in the disease-causing toxin PPIX, with additional benefit for patients receiving the 60 mg dose continuouslyTreatment with bitopertin was associated with sustained, significant improvement in average light tolerance and time to prodrome measuresBitopertin exhibited a favorable longer-term safety profile with up to 2.5+ years of exposure and similar safety across adults and adolescents with EPP and XLP

catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 2 anemia responses in myelofibrosis
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated Phase 2 RALLY-MF data in myelofibrosis with anemia showed durable anemia responses across transfusion-dependent and independent subgroups, with or without JAK inhibitor therapy. Clinically meaningful hemoglobin gains, transfusion independence in many patients, and improved patient-reported outcomes support therapeutic activity with a generally well-tolerated safety profile.
catalyst_text_evidence: Data from the RALLY-MF trial of DISC-0974 in patients with MF and anemia, to be presented in an oral session today, demonstrate meaningful, durable overall anemia responses across all patient subgroups, regardless of baseline transfusion status or concomitant JAK inhibitor use. The updated results demonstrated: Consistent, substantial decreases in hepcidin reaching >75% reduction from baseline and corresponding increases in serum iron 55% (N=17 of 31) of baseline nTD patients achieved a hemoglobin increase of ≥1.5 g/dL for ≥12 weeks (major response) and 68% had an increase of ≥1 g/dL for ≥12 weeks (overall response) 64% (N=7 of 11) of TD Low patients achieved transfusion independence (TI, major response) over a 16-week period and 73% achieved a ≥50% reduction in transfusions (overall response) 50% (N=4 of 8) of TD High patients achieved transfusion independence (TI, major response) over a 12-week period and 88% achieved a ≥50% reduction in transfusion requirement (overall response) 56% of patients receiving concomitant JAK inhibitor therapy achieved a major hematologic response across transfusion groups and 72% achieved an overall response, with similar response rates regardless of which specific JAK inhibitor the patient received DISC-0974 was generally well-tolerated.

catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 2 data in myelofibrosis anemia
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated Phase 2 RALLY-MF results were presented showing meaningful, durable anemia responses in myelofibrosis across non-transfusion-dependent and transfusion-dependent cohorts, with or without concomitant JAK inhibitors. Responses included substantial hemoglobin increases and high rates of transfusion independence, with a generally well-tolerated safety profile.
catalyst_text_evidence: WATERTOWN, Mass., 2026-06-02 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Disc Medicine, Inc. (NASDAQ:IRON), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of novel treatments for patients suffering from serious hematologic diseases, today presents updated data from the RALLY-MF Phase 2 trial of DISC-0974 in anemia of MF at the ASCO Annual Meeting in Chicago, IL. In this updated data set, treatment with DISC-0974 shows substantial reductions in hepcidin and increases in iron levels translating to positive impact on clinically meaningful measures of anemia across a broad range of patient types. 55% (N=17 of 31) of baseline nTD patients achieved a hemoglobin increase of ≥1.5 g/dL for ≥12 weeks (major response) and 68% had an increase of ≥1 g/dL for ≥12 weeks (overall response). 64% (N=7 of 11) of TD Low patients achieved transfusion independence (TI, major response) over a 16-week period and 73% achieved a ≥50% reduction in transfusions (overall response). 50% (N=4 of 8) of TD High patients achieved transfusion independence (TI, major response) over a 12-week period and 88% achieved a ≥50% reduction in transfusion requirement (overall response). DISC-0974 was generally well-tolerated.

catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 2 anemia data at ASH
detailed_catalyst_text: Initial data from a Phase 2 study in myelofibrosis-associated anemia were presented at a major hematology conference. Results showed substantial hepcidin reductions, increased iron, and meaningful anemia responses across transfusion statuses and with or without JAK inhibitor use. The findings support further development for an area with significant unmet need.
catalyst_text_evidence: WATERTOWN, Mass., 2025-12-06 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Disc Medicine, Inc. (NASDAQ:IRON) ... today presented positive initial data from the RALLY-MF Phase 2 trial of DISC-0974 in anemia of MF at the ASH Annual Meeting in Orlando, FL. The data demonstrated that treatment with DISC-0974 resulted in substantial reductions in hepcidin and increases in iron levels translating to positive impact on clinically meaningful measures of anemia across a broad range of patient types.

catalyst_text: A Type C meeting was held in coordination with the FDA regarding the use of PPIX reduction as a surrogate endpoint for the possible expedited approval of bitopertin, as noted on January 21, 2025.

An updated analysis from the Phase 2 trial presented at ASH indicated that bitopertin decreased PPIX in all predefined subgroups based on demographic and baseline patient characteristics, as reported on December 9, 2024.

Data from Phase 2, shared at ASH, indicated that bitopertin led to a significant decrease in protoporphyrin IX (PPIX) across both low and high doses, affecting both adult and adolescent groups, as reported on December 9, 2024.

drug_indication: Patients with non-dialysis dependent chronic kidney disease (NDD-CKD) and anemia
catalyst_text: Data from Phase 1b/2 presented at ASN showed that administering a single dose leads to prolonged suppression of hepcidin, promotes iron mobilization, and enhances erythropoiesis along with hemoglobin levels in NDD-CKD.

Data from Phase 1 involving healthy volunteers, presented at EHA, indicated that a mean serum iron reduction exceeding 50% from baseline was attained for both the 150-mg and 300-mg doses, as reported on June 14, 2024.
